name: Epher
overview: Epher was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Ezrah. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or narrative details provided. As a descendant within Judah, Epher is part of the broader lineage important to biblical history.
namesAndTitles: The name Epher means "[small] gazelle," reflecting a proper name given in Hebrew culture. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries the cultural significance typical of Hebrew personal names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Epher was the son of Ezrah, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections or relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Epher's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 4:17. While he does not have a detailed narrative or specific actions attributed to him, his place in the lineage contributes to the biblical understanding of Judah's descendants. This genealogical mention helps preserve the historical and tribal identity important to the biblical record.
